description: Find Wayback Machine snapshots of a URL. Mode "closest" returns the single nearest capture to a given timestamp, or the latest capture when timestamp is omitted, via the Availability API, falling back to a CDX closest-capture query when the Availability API finds no capture or answers with a rate limit, a server error, an unreadable response, or an error in place of a capture (one result). Mode "history" returns the full capture list via the CDX API — filterable by date range and HTTP status code, collapsed by default to one capture per day (collapse "timestamp:8"); collapse "timestamp:14" lists one row per distinct capture second. Use history mode to survey how a page changed over time; use closest mode when you need the snapshot nearest a specific date. History mode returns up to limit records (at most 10,000 per call) and supports resume-key pagination for URLs with very large capture histories.

collapse.description: CDX collapse parameter (history mode only). Format: "timestamp:N" where N is 1–14 (4=year, 6=month, 8=day, 10=hour, 14=second): consecutive captures sharing the first N timestamp digits are listed once. Omitted or blank, it is "timestamp:8", one capture per day. Pass "timestamp:14" for one row per distinct capture second.

from.description: Start of the date range (history mode only): 1–14 digits — YYYYMMDDHHMMSS or a prefix of it — or an ISO 8601 date or UTC date-time such as "2020-01-01". A prefix starts at the beginning of the period it names: "2015" is January 1, 2015.

limit.description: Maximum number of CDX records to return (history mode only, default 100). One call returns at most 10,000: a larger value (up to 150,000) is served as 10,000, and the resume_key continues from there.

mode.description: Lookup mode: "closest" returns the single nearest snapshot to the given timestamp, or the latest capture when timestamp is omitted; "history" returns the paginated full capture list via the CDX API.

resume_key.description: Opaque pagination key from a previous history mode response. Pass this to continue from where the last page left off. Server cursors expire after one hour and bind the URL and original filters; omit filters on continuation or repeat their original values. Page size may change. Wildcard and legacy raw continuations can omit collapsed captures.

status_filter.description: Filter CDX results to a specific HTTP status code (history mode only). Must be a 3-digit numeric code. Example: "200" to return only successful captures.

timestamp.description: Target timestamp for mode "closest": 1–14 digits — YYYYMMDDHHMMSS or a prefix of it, such as "20200615" — or an ISO 8601 date or UTC date-time such as "2020-06-15" or "2020-06-15T12:34:56Z". A shorter value names a period and resolves to the capture nearest its end: "2015" can resolve to one from early January 2016. Omitted or blank, it is the timestamp of a Wayback capture URL passed as url, else the latest capture.

to.description: End of the date range (history mode only), in the same forms as from, and inclusive: a prefix ends at the end of the period it names, so "2015" reaches December 31, 2015, and "20231231" the end of that day.

url.description: The URL to look up in the Wayback Machine. A Wayback capture URL — web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>/<url>, such as a replay_url — reads as the URL it archives: history mode lists that URL's captures, and closest mode looks up its timestamp, where a timestamp naming a different one fails as ambiguous_timestamp.

name: ia_find_snapshots

cap.description: The limit applied: limit, or 10,000 when a larger value was capped.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_resume_key`: The server history cursor is malformed, expired, or unavailable for this caller. `resume_key_conflict`: An explicit URL or filter conflicts with the server history cursor. `invalid_timestamp`: timestamp (closest mode), from, or to (history mode) is not 1–14 digits or an ISO 8601 date or UTC date-time, or names a month, day, hour, minute, or second no Gregorian date and time has; or url is a Wayback capture URL whose timestamp is not 1–14 digits naming a real date and time (field "url"). `ambiguous_timestamp`: Closest mode: url is a Wayback capture URL and timestamp names a different timestamp than the one the URL carries. `no_snapshots`: No snapshots found for the given URL with the current filters. `no_snapshot_available`: Closest mode: no capture exists near the requested timestamp for this URL, or, with no timestamp, none exists at all. Either mode: the Wayback Machine does not serve captures of this URL at all — the CDX or Availability API answered HTTP 403, 410, or 451, as it does for a site excluded from the archive. `cdx_unavailable`: The Wayback CDX API answered HTTP 5xx after retries or 429, refused the request with another 4xx, did not answer within the request timeout, could not be reached, returned an unreadable response, or did not finish within the call's 55 s deadline (the request timeout when that is longer); in closest mode, the Availability API found no capture and the CDX closest-capture check it fell back to failed, did not complete in time, or had no time left. `availability_unavailable`: Closest mode: the Wayback Availability API answered HTTP 429, or 408, 425, or 5xx after retries, an unreadable response, or an error in place of a capture, and the CDX closest-capture check it fell back to failed too or had no time left within the call's 55 s deadline (the request timeout when that is longer); or the Availability API refused the request with another 4xx, did not answer within the request timeout or that deadline, or could not be reached, none of which falls back. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Pagination guidance, cap disclosure, or limitations of legacy raw continuation.

resume_key.description: Opaque key to pass as resume_key in the next call to continue paginating CDX history results.

snapshots.description: List of snapshots matching the query.

items.description: A single Wayback Machine snapshot record.

digest.description: SHA-1 digest of the content (history mode).

mimetype.description: MIME type of the captured content (history mode).

replay_url.description: Full Wayback Machine replay URL for this snapshot.

statuscode.description: HTTP status code at time of capture ("-" for a revisit record).

truncated.description: True when the snapshot list was capped at the limit.

title: Find Wayback Machine Snapshots
